motion_rule: the tray drives her down the aisle right to left every beat and she is never taken off it; crates and ice sweep across the lens a fin away; the camera tracks alongside at her height; new shot size each beat, never wider than her head filling a third of frame; ONE sideways move per window, never up or down, never a chain
character: a plump mackerel with a mirror-striped flank, lying along the tray, jaw working, eye always clear
second_characters: ONE heavy seller in a stained apron, gold teeth, running level with the tray a shoulder away from 6.45 and crossing the lens himself; ONE buyer, arms only, at 7.60
props: A SWARM of grey salmon heads dumped in a battered soup crate; ONE fat roll of banknotes; ONE fish bone behind his ear
prop_continuity: the heads stay in the crate from 1.90; the bone leaves his ear at 7.05
environment: a fish hall, daylight from the roof, tiled counters and packed crates a fin away both sides, no far wall
light_events: flat white noon off the tiles, a mirror flash down her flank at 3.75

audio.language: Russian, lines verbatim; latin hints never spoken
audio.delivery: a smug oily female voice, biting each word, 4.5 syllables/sec
audio.pronunciation: prosh-LI, vre-me-NA, lo-SO-sya, te-PER, O-che-red, blis-TAT, KAZH-doy, KOS-toch-ke
audio.pacing: 0.00-1.90, 2.15-4.25 and 4.50-6.45 each one breath; after 6.45 not a word, sfx keep going
audio.lip_sync: her jaw opens wide and shapes every syllable
audio.sfx: ice crunching, trays scraping, crates banging, running boots, a wet guffaw

timeline.a: the tray shoves off and drives her past a crate raking the lens
she rides on, ice sheeting off the tray past the lens
her tail whips and hurls the grey salmon heads off the tray into the crate
the heads crash in the crate and he boots it across the lens
she shoulders the last ice off the tray past the lens
she throws her body over, the tray skidding on under her
she drives her flank at the lens, crates banging past both sides
the tray swerves and her striped flank rips across the lens
the tray hits a rut, ice jumping sideways off it
she leans in at the lens, jaw wide, the aisle tearing past
the tray slams through a rut, ice and water sheeting across the lens
she throws her flank at the lens, crates ripping past both sides
he tears in level with the tray and swipes melt off her ice past the lens
still running he pulls the bone from behind his ear and flicks it across the lens
the buyer arms catch the bone and shove the roll past the lens, he snatches it on the run
he rams the roll inside his apron and guffaws into the lens, the tray driving her past him
she whips her tail and slaps ice past the lens at him
she drives past the last crates, jaw working

must_appear: she stays on the moving tray to the last frame, never lifted, never carried; he never touches her, runs level with her and never stops; every line is spoken, the last word by 6.45; from 6.45 the order runs melt, bone, roll, apron, guffaw, one to a beat
negative_prompt: subtitles, watermark, letterbox, night, dark scene, cyrillic letters, words, digits, a price card, a parked camera, a standing seller, a fish lifted off the tray, a fish in a bag, weighing scales, a hero moving up or down the frame, a closed jaw while speaking, slow motion, an empty aisle, a word not in the lines
